$comment: SPTR model registry — the single authoritative answer to 'which model is actually deployed'.
ML-F1 is why this file exists. The ML strategy document described a 29-class v2 as 'the
bundled TFLite model'. The APK ships a 10-class v1 that cannot abstain at all. Two model
versions existed, both measured, and nothing in the repository recorded which one was
deployed — so a reader planning from the strategy believed abstention work was partly done
in the product when it was not started.
1. Nothing here is fabricated. A value that is not known is stated as UNKNOWN,
NOT_RECORDED or LEGACY, and that absence is itself the useful evidence.
2. `deployment_status` is the field the CI fence checks against the actual asset tree.
Editing it without editing reality makes the build fail, which is the point.
3. TRAINED does not imply EVALUATED. EVALUATED does not imply CHALLENGER.
CHALLENGER does not imply CHAMPION. Promotion is always a separate decision.
4. This registry is not evidence that any model works, and no entry in it changes D1.

models.task: single-label image classification of gym equipment
models.architecture: MobileNetV2 (ImageNet weights) + 10-way softmax head, float16 quantised
models.training_code_location: D:/tools/equipment-model (NOT under version control — verified: no .git)
models.training_dataset_description: 1741 web-crawled photos, deduped by pixel hash, 115-200 per class
models.input_schema_version: float32 [1,224,224,3], raw 0-255; [-1,1] scaling inside the graph, so metadata declares mean 0 / std 1
models.abstention_note: A closed 10-way softmax over a 69-machine catalogue. It cannot say 'not a machine I know' — probability mass is redistributed over the ten it has. B1 measured its three most confident real-world answers as all wrong, up to 0.897, on machines it has no class for. No confidence threshold repairs this; it is a property of the head, not of the threshold.

evaluations.dataset: held-out 15% stratified slice of the same web crawl
evaluations.caveat: Same distribution as training: catalogue-style photos, clean background, machine centred. An upper bound, not a product number.
The real-world measurement. Not a single frame was rejected by either shipped threshold, and the live threshold (0.05) is below random for ten classes (0.10).

guardrail_metrics.confident_false_identification: PRESENT — measured up to 0.897 on out-of-catalogue machines

models.fallback: machine_text_anchor (OCR of the machine's printed name) — measured 18/18 where a name is legible, and the stronger anchor of the two
models.rollback_note: No previous version exists. This is v1.
models.notes: Champion by default rather than by evaluation: it is the only model that has ever shipped. Its provenance is partial — the training code is not under version control, so `training_code_commit` cannot be resolved and this model cannot be regenerated by anyone who does not hold that directory.

models.task: single-label image classification of gym equipment, with abstention
models.training_dataset_description: 55,466 crops from CC BY 4.0 Roboflow datasets (36 usable of 112 found), bounding-box cropped, with background crops mined for the `none` class from photos that contain a recognised machine
models.abstention_note: `none` is a real trained class, not a threshold. Measured: it corrected two of B1's confident errors (the abduction machine went from `treadmill` 0.892 to `none` 0.808). NOT yet stable under viewpoint — the same abdominal machine reads `treadmill` 0.940 from one angle and `none` 0.946 from another.

evaluations.dataset: operator's 30 real gym photos — 18 labelled with certainty, 12 wide room shots not gradable by a one-label classifier
evaluations.caveat: 28% top-3 is not a product. Measured against the only real-world sample the project has.

models.challenger_note: Deliberately NOT marked challenger. A challenger is a formal state reached by passing an evaluation gate, and no gate has been run: there is no independent held-out set (ML_STRATEGY step M0 is unstarted), and its one real-world number is worse than a product bar. It is an EXPERIMENTAL model. Calling it a challenger because it is newer is exactly the drift this registry exists to stop.
models.notes: The ML strategy document described this as 29 classes; the artefact's own labels.json lists 37 including `none`. The registry records the measured value. D3 remains in force: nothing here authorises shipping v2.

models.architecture: deterministic rule set; no learned parameters
models.$artifact_note: Source, not a binary. The sha256/bytes fields are null because hashing a text file that git already versions would be a second, worse version-control system. The dataset manifest records the commit the baseline ran at, which is the reproducibility claim that matters here.
models.$training_code_commit_note: NOT 'UNKNOWN'. The exact commit is recorded per build in core/ml/datasets/<dataset>/manifest.json under source_commit, and is resolvable there. Writing a commit into this file would be a self-reference -- the commit that contains the registry cannot be known while writing it -- which is a trap this programme already fell into once with a report's own HEAD.
models.training_code_location: scripts/ct1/ in this repository, under version control
models.$training_dataset_note: A rule set is not trained, so it has no training dataset. It is EVALUATED against content_qa_catalogue v1 (see evaluations).
models.training_dataset_description: none; the baseline has no learned parameters
models.input_schema_version: catalogue row, exercises_vendor.json schema as of dataset content_qa_catalogue v1
models.output_schema: Label{item_id, check, source, value, evidence} per scripts/ct1/label_contract.py
models.abstention_note: Abstains by construction: it emits a finding only when a stated condition holds, and says nothing about every row it does not flag. Silence here means 'no rule matched', never 'this row is fine' -- 56% of the catalogue is unflagged and none of it has been reviewed.

evaluations.$metrics_note: EVALUATION_LABEL_GAP. There are zero human-reviewed QA labels in this repository, so precision and recall cannot be computed against any ground truth. A number derived from the baseline's own output would measure it against itself.

guardrail_metrics.$note: The baseline reads the catalogue and emits findings. It has no write path to any catalogue, taxonomy or user-facing surface, and CT-1 promotion does not grant one.

models.rollback_note: First champion for this task. There is nothing behind it, and the deterministic rules are themselves the floor a challenger has to clear -- so the rollback for any future ML challenger is this entry.
models.notes: CT-1. The champion is deliberately a rule set: an ML challenger must beat exact rules on reviewer workload and novel-defect yield, and imitating them is not beating them. See core/ml/CT1_CONTENT_QA.md.

vendor_models.$comment: Third-party models the app depends on but does not train. Listed so the registry is a complete answer to 'what models run', and excluded from the CI fence because we neither version nor bundle them.

entries.note: The pose model is the vendor's. The rep counter on top of it is ours and has never been measured — ML_STRATEGY §1.2 shows the published accuracy figures came from a different algorithm (3D/bilateral/2-phase) than the one that ships (2D/one-side/4-phase).
Measured 18/18 where a machine's printed name is legible — the strongest recognition signal in the product, and not a model we train.
Provider moderation is configured (F026) and closes nothing in the fitness-safety space.
